overview.overview:
Nebraska's 1st District, anchored in Lincoln and surrounding eastern Nebraska, is a reliably Republican seat at the presidential level. The district backed Donald Trump by roughly 15 points in 2020 and by about 13 points in 2024, sitting well to the right of the nation as a whole. Its single electoral vote, awarded separately under Nebraska's system, is therefore expected to stay in the Republican column in 2028.

The forecast expects a Republican margin of about 8.5 points, an improvement for Republicans relative to 2024 given the anticipated national environment. The wide uncertainty range reflects the district's small size and the possibility of larger-than-usual swings, but even the favorable end of that range only reaches a narrow Democratic edge.
overview.watch: A major national swing toward Democrats well beyond current expectations would be needed to put this electoral vote genuinely in play.
key_factors: The district's strong Republican lean, roughly 13 points right of the nation
A favorable national environment for Republicans in 2028
Lincoln's Democratic-leaning vote as the main counterweight
Nebraska's split allocation of electoral votes making this single vote distinct
